_comment: Which scene holds which texture, for analysis/texture_dataset.py.
Copy to texture_classes.json and replace with the scenes as they come off the Pi.
A class may list SEVERAL scenes -- that is how one texture recorded over two sessions stays
one label -- but a scene must not appear under two classes.
Read this before trusting a result: when a class is exactly one scene, the classifier can
reach the label through anything that scene did differently (lighting, time of day, where the
rig sat) instead of through the texture. Two scenes per class, recorded at different times,
is what makes a high score mean the texture. If every class is one scene, treat the number as
an upper bound and say so.
